decisions.decision: Does MACOS_SETUP_CONFIG_PATH have a default path?
decisions.ruling: No. When MACOS_SETUP_CONFIG_PATH is unset or empty, setup_sync stops with exit 2 and names the variable. When the folder does not exist, it also stops with exit 2. The macos-setup tool sets the variable in its generated mise config (P10).
decisions.rejected: A default path, for example the iCloud folder of the old engine or ~/Projects/github.com/<user>/macos-setup.

decisions.decision: Which keys does a Mac tools.toml accept?
decisions.ruling: description, stage and depends (each optional; depends defaults to []), [defaults], [questions.<key>], [contributes.<tool>], [files."<target>"] and [mise.*]. The repo-only keys default_envs, root_only, extensions, [[precommit]] and [mise_env.*], and requires_found in a [files] table, stop the run with exit 2 and a message that says the key is for repo tools only. Any other key also stops the run with exit 2.
decisions.rejected: The five required keys of a repo tools.toml on the Mac side too.

decisions.decision: Where does the [mise.*] config of macos.toml go?
decisions.ruling: U1 calls the own-config entry of sync-engine/mise (P08 item 7), which generates the [mise.*] tables of macos.toml into ~/.config/mise/conf.d/zz-macos/mise.toml with the header `# Synced from bootstrap: macos.toml [mise]. Do not edit this file.` and `# The next sync replaces it, and a manual change is lost.` U1 does not build the file itself. setup-sync writes it in the main stage, and its manifest line is `zz-macos<TAB>.config/mise/conf.d/zz-macos/mise.toml`. A Mac tool folder named zz-macos, or one whose name sorts after zz-macos in byte order, stops the run with exit 2.
decisions.rejected: The init stage (the user config starts no shell); a file without the header (the stale rule cannot remove it).

decisions.decision: What is the template context on the Mac side?
decisions.ruling: .config (the values of the tool), .all (the values of every selected tool, by name), .tools (the selected tool names), .env (HOME, USER and MACOS_SETUP_CONFIG_PATH) and .sync_engine (the absolute path of the sync-engine/ folder of SYNC_ENGINE_CLONE, as the repo front-end gives it since P01). The delimiters are <% %>.
decisions.rejected: Keep MACOS_SETUP_REPO_PATH in .env: no Mac repo clone exists now, and no template reads it.

decisions.decision: What happens when the config folder has no macos.toml?
decisions.ruling: Port the rule of the old engine: setup-sync selects pack base and its depends only. A clean real run then calls _se_record_commit (P02 item 9) with the new-file header `# The values of the Mac sync of bootstrap. See docs/setup/index.md.`, which creates macos.toml with that header and the bootstrap_commit line. A symlinked macos.toml is written through to its real file.

decisions.decision: Can U1 change a shared library?
decisions.ruling: No. U1 edits only sync-engine/setup-sync. Each Mac-only step (the symlink resolve, the stages, the login shell check, mise bootstrap, the mise path check) is a function in setup-sync that calls the shared libraries. When a library has no entry that a wrapper can use, U1 returns UNRESOLVED and names the missing entry.
decisions.rejected: Edit sync-engine/common, write, select, values, merge, manifest or mise in this plan.

decisions.ruling: In setup_sync, as its first check after the flags. The check and its message are the ones of the old entry task, so a ~/.local/bin/mise link into another folder also fails.
decisions.rejected: Only in the entry task (P10): then a direct call of the engine skips the check.

decisions.decision: How does test:setup-sync run the engine?
decisions.ruling: Each case makes a git copy of the fixture tree (sync-engine/ of the working tree, plus macos/fixtures/repo/ as macos/), sets SYNC_ENGINE_CLONE to it, sources its sync-engine/setup-sync and calls setup_sync. The clone, the lock and the temp copy belong to the entry task (P10), so the old clone and lock cases go to P10.
decisions.rejected: Run the cases through an entry task, which does not exist before P10.

decisions.decision: Which macos-setup tool does the fixture tree use?
decisions.ruling: A minimal fixture tool macos/fixtures/repo/tools/macos-setup/ with a tools.toml that has only a description. Pack base of the fixture packs.toml holds it with default = true.
decisions.rejected: A copy of the real macos/tools/macos-setup/, which P10 creates.

decisions.ruling: Dropped: the iCloud cases (dataless, dataless timeout, bad timeout) with the stat stub; the clone cases, the lock cases and the cases that run the old _default, which P10 ports to the entry task; and the case "a <tool>.toml of a tool that is not selected", because its rule is gone. A case whose rule exists in a new form is rewritten to that form. 02-tests.md lists each old case and its fate in a table.
decisions.rejected: Keep the stat stub and the iCloud cases.

decisions.decision: How do the messages name the values?
decisions.ruling: Each message keeps the `setup-sync: ` prefix of the log function. A message that named <tool>.toml, [overrides.<tool>] or macos-setup.toml now names [tools.<tool>] of macos.toml, or macos.toml.
decisions.rejected: Keep the old file names in the messages.

decisions.decision: Does the plan need a review unit?
decisions.ruling: Yes. U1 adds sync-engine/setup-sync and U2 adds two task scripts, and all of them run. One review unit in wave 3 covers U1 and U2.
decisions.rejected: No review unit: the wave review alone does not run /security-review.

decisions.decision: Can this plan run in parallel with another plan of the chain?
decisions.ruling: No. The 16 plans form one linear chain through requires, because most of them edit sync-engine/repo-sync or sync-engine/setup-sync, and parallel plans conflict there.

decisions.decision: Where do the tests of this plan go?
decisions.ruling: In this plan: U2 ports the old setup-sync test and adds cases for the new rules. No existing test of test:repo-sync changes.

decisions.decision: Does the plan run setup:configs or the Mac sync?
decisions.ruling: No. mise run setup:configs in bootstrap and in consumers, and the first Mac run, stay hand steps (Out of scope).
decisions.rejected: A unit or an after-landing step that runs them.

decisions.decision: Does the Mac stale rule follow symlinks?
decisions.ruling: Yes. U1 calls sync-engine/manifest with the link mode macos (P05 item 5): the stale rule resolves links, removes the real file, then removes empty parents up to $HOME, never past a symlinked folder. On the Mac, ~/.config/mise is a link into dotfiles/, and the mise config of a deselected tool must go. The old case "a stale file through a link" stays. U1 passes the mode and edits no library (D6).
decisions.rejected: The repo link mode, which never removes a path behind a link.

decisions.decision: What does a failed file in the init stage do?
decisions.ruling: The rule of the old engine stays (B:1564-1580): a failure in the init stage stops the run before the main stage, with no mise bootstrap and no manifest write. Inside one stage, a failed file stops no other file.
decisions.rejected: Go on with the main stage after a failed init stage.

gaps.text: Edit 1.6 validates tools.toml for every folder, but the [questions] rules in sync-engine/values reach selected tools only · assumed the manifest template of the old engine stays and checks [defaults], [questions] and [contributes] shapes for every tool, so a bad table in an unselected tool still returns 2

the plan does not say whether a mise depends of a Mac [mise.tools] entry adds the tool that defines it, or whether two Mac tools may define one mise tool · assumed the Mac closure follows only the tools.toml depends key, with no duplicate check
the table says the merge cases are fourteen, but the old test has 16 (12 behaviour, 4 config errors) · assumed all were meant, and all 16 are ported
the table and edit 4 both list an override path that no selected tool has · assumed two cases are wanted, the second uses its own folder override-none

Edit 1.11 and D4 never require a rendered value to be encoded in a .tmpl target, so a string with a quote and a newline in [tools.<name>] of macos.toml can add tables or keys to a rendered TOML, JSON or YAML target (setup-sync:601; no privilege gain, the same author can write [mise.*]) · the run encoded the strings of the fixture templates; the rule goes into CLAUDE.md through U4, and the real Mac templates of P11 to P14 must follow it; those approved plans were not edited by this run

handed to the docs unit U4, whose file does not name them: CLAUDE.md:115 the member order of a pack is the sync order holds only for repo-sync; CLAUDE.md:220 the Mac front-end is not in this repository yet; the CLAUDE.md sync-engine/ list and README.md:51 lack setup-sync; CLAUDE.md its only test is test:repo-sync, and the Layout list lacks macos/fixtures/ and the two test tasks; add the rule that a TOML, JSON or YAML template encodes a string value with data.ToJSON · open until U4 lands them · closed: U4 landed each line in 433503f
